picks.title: Around the Book World: MVB builds Snackz AI metadata into its system; AI-assisted Czech audio; AI floods strain KDP print-on-demand
picks.excerpt: Carlo Carrenho's weekly roundup: Germany's MVB is building Snackz's AI tool into its system to generate classifications, keywords and SEO copy from manuscripts or book proposals. ElredoVoice is bringing 20 HarperCollins Polska Harlequin titles into Czech audio with AI-assisted production. The roundup also looks at how AI floods pressure Amazon KDP's print-on-demand pipeline.
picks.rationale: The freshest item, and the most actionable: AI metadata generation is going into Germany's core book-data infrastructure. The lead story (MVB/Snackz) has not been published before; the 09-21 roundup was dropped because its Spotify lead repeats the 09-13 card.

picks.title: Publishing's AI stance is pushing authors into a culture of secrecy
picks.excerpt: Author and editor Madeleine F White argues that publishing's stance on AI is pushing writers into a culture of secrecy. If the industry wants transparency about AI use, she says, it has to make honesty safer than concealment.
picks.rationale: A fresh (09-28) argument on AI-disclosure policy from a reputable trade outlet. Earlier Bookseller comments covered different topics (illustrators, licensing, author AI policies); this is a new piece, not a repeat URL.

picks.title: Soundgrab and Voicegrab launch a 'hybrid cinema audiobook' format pairing AI voices with film-grade mixing
picks.excerpt: Post-production studio Soundgrab and AI voice company Voicegrab are launching a 'hybrid cinema audiobook' format that pairs AI voice technology with film-grade sound mixing, and have hired a Hollywood re-recording mixer. The startups are tenants of Korea's NIPA Virtual Convergence Industry Hub.
picks.rationale: A concrete new format for AI audiobook production. No earlier card covers Soundgrab or Voicegrab (the 09-24 mt.co.kr card was about AI web-novel spam).

picks.title: 21-year translator tells National Assembly Library panel AI translation is unsustainable without humans
picks.excerpt: Noh Seung-young, a translator with 21 years in the field, told a National Assembly Library expert panel that AI machine translation 'is not sustainable even in the short term' without human intervention. He warns that translators are being asked to do more intensive post-editing work for less pay.
picks.rationale: First-hand evidence of how MT post-editing is changing translators' labour and pay in Korean publishing. It is distinct from the 09-26 Manga Plus survey card and the 09-18 PW translation piece.

picks.title: 'Grandmaslop': grandparents are making personalised AI storybooks, and parents hate them
picks.excerpt: 'Grandmaslop': grandparents are using Gemini, Claude and ChatGPT to make whole personalised AI storybooks starring their grandchildren. Parents on Reddit say the books share the same slop cartoon style and stories with broken meter, a sign of how cheap AI children's-book generation is changing what counts as a picture book.
picks.rationale: A new consumer-side trend in AI picture-book generation, with a visual and style angle. It is distinct from the 08-30 Creative Bloq children's-book opinion piece, and it adds a fourth outlet type (consumer tech).
